summary: In the November 2026 Visa Bulletin, F4 (Brothers and Sisters of Adult U.S. Citizens) Final Action Dates advanced for 2 of 5 chargeability areas and held steady for 3.
The largest move was for All other countries, up 366 days (≈12.0 months) to Oct 22, 2012. China (mainland-born) moved by the same amount to the same date.
India, Mexico and the Philippines had no change.
For November 2026, USCIS is using the Dates for Filing chart (Table B) for family-sponsored I-485 filings.

sections.heading: F4 Final Action Dates advanced for All other countries and China in November 2026
paragraphs: The F4 Final Action Date (Table A) for All other countries moved from Oct 22, 2011 in October 2026 to Oct 22, 2012 in November 2026. That is an advance of 366 days (≈12.0 months). China (mainland-born) shows the same change: Oct 22, 2011 to Oct 22, 2012, also 366 days (≈12.0 months).
Three areas did not move. India stayed at Dec 15, 2006, Mexico stayed at Apr 22, 2001, and the Philippines stayed at May 15, 2008.

sections.heading: F4 Dates for Filing (Table B) and how far they are ahead of Final Action Dates
paragraphs: For November 2026, USCIS says family-sponsored applicants use the Dates for Filing chart (Table B) for Form I-485. If your priority date is earlier than the Table B date for your category and country, you may be able to file your adjustment of status application this month. Other eligibility requirements still apply.

F4 Table B dates for November 2026: All other countries Nov 1, 2012; China (mainland-born) Nov 1, 2012; India Feb 1, 2007; Mexico Apr 30, 2001; Philippines Mar 22, 2009. Compared with October 2026, All other countries and China (mainland-born) each advanced 366 days (≈12.0 months) from Nov 1, 2011. India, Mexico and the Philippines had no change in Table B.

Table B is later than Table A in every F4 column. The gap is 10 days (≈0.3 months) for All other countries, 10 days (≈0.3 months) for China (mainland-born), 48 days (≈1.6 months) for India, 8 days (≈0.3 months) for Mexico, and 311 days (≈10.2 months) for the Philippines.

sections.heading: F4 Final Action Date record over the last 6 and 12 bulletins
paragraphs: This history covers Final Action Dates (Table A) only. For All other countries and China (mainland-born), the last 6 bulletins (since May 2026) show a move from Sep 15, 2008 to Oct 22, 2012, a net gain of 1498 days (≈49.2 months), with advances in 5 bulletins and no change in 1. Over the last 12 bulletins (since November 2025), the date moved from Jan 8, 2008 to Oct 22, 2012, net +1749 days (≈57.5 months), advancing in 7 and unchanged in 5. Neither retrogressed in that period.

India moved from Nov 1, 2006 to Dec 15, 2006 over both periods, net +44 days (≈1.4 months). It advanced in 1 of the last 6 bulletins and 1 of the last 12. Mexico moved from Apr 8, 2001 to Apr 22, 2001, net +14 days (≈0.5 months), also advancing in 1 of 6 and 1 of 12.

The Philippines advanced in 3 of the last 6 bulletins, from Jul 15, 2007 to May 15, 2008 (net +305 days, ≈10.0 months). Over the last 12 bulletins, it advanced in 8 and was unchanged in 4, moving from Mar 22, 2006 to May 15, 2008 (net +785 days, ≈25.8 months). No F4 area retrogressed in either period.

faq.a: It is Mar 22, 2009, unchanged from October 2026. That is 311 days (≈10.2 months) later than the Philippines F4 Final Action Date of May 15, 2008.
